**1 Kings 8:1–66**

1. Now it came to pass, when Solomon had finished building the house of the Lord and the king’s house, that Solomon made a solemn assembly of the elders of Israel and all the heads of the tribes, the leaders of the fathers' houses of the children of Israel, in Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of the covenant of the Lord from the city of David, which is Zion.

2. And they brought up the ark from the city of David, and all the Levites carried the tabernacle of the testimony, and the vessels that were in it, and the priests and the Levites brought them up.

3. And the king and all the men of Judah and Israel, the kings and the priests, and the Levites, and the leaders of the fathers' houses of Israel, the heads of the families, came to Jerusalem.

4. And Solomon brought up the daughter of Pharaoh from the city of David to the house that he had built for her, for he said, "Let the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and the tabernacle of the testimony, and the altar of burnt offering, come into this house." And Solomon did not bring up the ark of the covenant of the Lord into the house of the Lord, into the holy of holies, until that time.

5. And the priests brought in the ark of the covenant of the Lord to its place, into the inner sanctuary of the house, to the most holy place, under the wings of the cherubim.

6. For the cherubim spread out their wings over the place of the ark, and the cherubim overshadowed the ark and its poles from above.

7. And the poles were so long that the ends of the poles were seen from the holy place before the inner sanctuary; yet they were not seen from outside. And they are there to this day.

8. There was nothing in the ark except the two stone tablets which Moses put there at Horeb, where the Lord made a covenant with the children of Israel, when they came out of the land of Egypt.

9. And it came to pass, when the priests had come out of the holy place, that the cloud filled the house of the Lord,

10. so that the priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud, for the glory of the Lord filled the house of the Lord.

11. Then Solomon said, "The Lord has said that He would dwell in thick darkness.

12. But I have built for You an exalted house, a place for You to dwell forever."

13. And the king turned his face and blessed all the assembly of Israel, and all the assembly of Israel stood.

14. And he said, "Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, who has spoken with His mouth to David my father, and with His hand has fulfilled it, saying,

15. Since the day that I brought My people Israel out of Egypt, I have not chosen a city out of all the tribes of Israel in which to build a house, that My name might be there; nor have I chosen any man to be a ruler over My people Israel.

16. But David my father took it to his heart to build a house for the name of the Lord, the God of Israel.

17. And the Lord said to David my father, 'Because it was in your heart to build a house for My name, you did well that you had this intention in your heart.

18. Yet you shall not build the house, but your son who will be born to you shall build the house for My name.'

19. And the Lord has fulfilled His word, which He spoke; for I have risen up in the place of David my father, and I have sat on the throne of Israel, as the Lord promised, and I have built the house for the name of the Lord, the God of Israel.

20. And I have prepared a place there for the ark, in which is the covenant of the Lord that He made with the children of Israel when He brought them out of the land of Egypt."

21. Then Solomon stood before the altar of the Lord in the presence of all the assembly of Israel, and he spread forth his hands toward heaven,

22. and said, "O Lord, God of Israel, there is no God like You in heaven above or on earth beneath, who keeps covenant and mercy with Your servants who walk before You with all their hearts,

23. who have kept with Your servant David my father what You promised him; indeed, You spoke with Your mouth, and with Your hand You have fulfilled it, as it is this day.

24. Now, O Lord, God of Israel, keep with Your servant David my father what You promised him, saying, 'You shall not lack a man before Me to sit on the throne of Israel, so long as your children take heed to their way to walk before Me as you have walked before Me.'

25. And now, O Lord, God of Israel, let Your word be fulfilled with Your servant David my father.

26. For can it be that God dwells on earth? Indeed, the heavens and the highest heavens cannot contain You. How much less this house that I have built!

27. Yet look to the prayer of Your servant and to his supplication, O Lord my God, and listen to the cry and to the prayer which Your servant prays before You this day,

28. that Your eyes may be open toward this house night and day, toward the place of which You said to me, 'My name shall be there,' that You may listen to the prayer which Your servant offers toward this place.

29. And listen to the supplications of Your servant and of Your people Israel, when they pray toward this place. And You shall hear from Your dwelling place, which is in heaven; and when You hear, You shall forgive.

30. If a man sins against his neighbor and is made to take an oath, and comes and takes an oath before Your altar in this house,

31. then hear from heaven and act, and judge Your servant, giving recompense to the wicked by bringing his conduct upon his own head, and justifying the righteous by giving him according to his righteousness.

32. And if Your people Israel are defeated before their enemies because they have sinned against You, and they turn back and confess Your name, and pray and make supplication before You in this house,

33. then hear from heaven and forgive the sin of Your people Israel, and bring them back to the land which You gave to their fathers.

34. When Your people are struck down before their enemies, and they pray to You toward this city which You have chosen, and toward the house which I have built for Your name,

35. then hear from heaven Your prayer and their supplications, and maintain their cause.

36. And when the sky is shut up and there is no rain because they have sinned against You, and they pray toward this place and confess Your name, and turn from their sin when You afflict them,

37. then hear from heaven and forgive the sin of Your servants and Your people Israel, teaching them the good way in which they should walk; and send rain on Your land, which You gave to Your people for an inheritance.

38. When there is famine or plague in the land, blight or mildew, locusts or grasshoppers; when their enemy besieges them in any of their cities, whatever plague, whatever sickness there is;

39. whatever prayer and supplication is made by any man, by all the people around him, when each one knows the wound of his own heart, and spreads out his hands toward this house;

40. then hear from Your dwelling place in heaven, and forgive, and act, and give to every man according to all his ways, whose heart You know (for You alone know the hearts of all the children of men),

41. that they may fear You all the days that they live in the land which You gave to our fathers.

42. And for the foreigner who is not of Your people Israel, but who comes from a distant land for the sake of Your great name and Your mighty hand and Your outstretched arm, when he comes and prays toward this house,

43. then hear from heaven Your dwelling place, and do according to all for which the foreigner calls to You, so that all the peoples of the earth may know Your name and fear You, as do Your people Israel, and that they may know that this house which I have built is called by Your name.

44. When Your people go out to battle against their enemies, by whatever way You send them, and they pray to the Lord toward the city which You have chosen and toward the house which I have built for Your name,

45. then hear from heaven their prayer and their supplication, and maintain their cause.

46. For they will sin against You (for there is no man who does not sin), and You will be angry with them and deliver them to the enemy, so that they may carry them away captive to the land far off or near.

47. Then when they come to themselves in the land to which they have been carried away captive, they will repent and make supplication to You in the land of their captivity, saying, "We have sinned, we have done wrong, we have committed iniquity."

48. And when they return to You with all their heart and with all their soul in the land of their captivity, where they have been carried away, and they pray to You toward their land which You gave to their fathers, the city which You chose, and toward the house which I have built for Your name,

49. then hear from heaven Your dwelling place their prayer and their supplications, and maintain their cause,

50. and forgive Your people who have sinned against You, and all their transgressions which they have transgressed against You, and grant them compassion in the sight of those who carried them away captive, that they may have compassion on them.

51. For they are Your people and Your inheritance, whom You brought out of the land of Egypt, out of the iron furnace.

52. Let Your eyes be open and Your ears attentive to the prayer of Your servant and to the prayer of Your people Israel, that You may listen to them whenever they pray to You."

53. Then Solomon made this prayer in the presence of the Lord at the dedication of the house of the Lord:

54. "The Lord has said that He would dwell in the clouds;

55. the Lord who made the heavens and the earth, the sea and all that is in them, who keeps faith forever, who executes justice for the oppressed, who gives food to the hungry. The Lord gives freedom to the captives, and opens the eyes of the blind. The Lord lifts up those who are bowed down; the Lord loves the righteous. The Lord watches over the sojourners; He upholds the orphan and the widow. And the Lord hates the wicked.

56. The Lord has established His covenant forever; He has made His promise firm to David.

57. So may the Lord our God be with us, as He was with our fathers; let Him not leave us nor forsake us,

58. that He may turn our hearts to Him, to walk in all His ways and to keep His commandments, His statutes, and His judgments, which He commanded our fathers.

59. And let these words of mine, with which I have made supplication before the Lord, be near to the Lord our God day and night, to do justice for His servant and for His people Israel, every day.

60. That all the peoples of the earth may know that the Lord is God; there is none else.

61. And let our hearts be wholly true to the Lord our God, to walk in His statutes and to keep His commandments as at this day."

62. Then the king and all Israel with him offered sacrifices before the Lord.

63. And Solomon offered as a peace offering to the Lord 22,000 oxen and 120,000 sheep. And the king and all the people of Israel dedicated the house of the Lord.

64. On that day the king consecrated the middle of the court that was before the house of the Lord, for there he offered the burnt offering, the grain offering, and the fat of the peace offerings; because the bronze altar that was before the Lord was too small to hold the burnt offering, the grain offering, and the fat of the peace offerings.

65. And Solomon held the feast at that time, and all Israel with him, a great assembly, from the entrance of Hamath to the Brook of Egypt, before the Lord our God, seven days and seven days, fourteen days.

66. And on the eighth day he sent the people away, and they blessed the king, and they went to their tents, joyful and glad of heart for all the good things that the Lord had done for David His servant and for Israel His people.
